# Part 3 source records: second sweep (6 lanes from Edwin's clarifications)

**Date:** 2026-09-29 · generated by `tools/evidence-check/build_part3_files.py` from the verified store; not edited by hand.

Each work was saved as full text and read by one agent, which locked every item to a line of the saved text with a short verbatim anchor. A script checked that each anchor occurs in the saved text and that the numbers of the item stand within three lines of it. A second agent, which did not write the record, then tried to refute each item against the text. Items shown here passed both checks. Where the auditor corrected an item, the corrected wording is shown and the Audit column says so. The verbatim anchors and the saved texts are kept outside the repository; this file gives the location of every item instead. Only works that are eligible under the source rule of 2026-09-29 (D313) are listed; the others are in the evidence ledger, section 1b.

Columns: # = item index (the reference is <record id>#<index>); Field = what the item is about; Line = line in the saved text of the version read. Full references: evidence ledger, References.

| 0 | mechanism | The survey's framework: a modern agent is a configuration coupling a foundation model with an operational scaffold of prompts, memory, tools and control logic; self-improvement is a self-induced update operator that obtains and commits updates to the model parameters or to scaffold components (formalized as A_t=(theta_t, Sigma_t), Eq. 1-2, and Eq. 4-6). | - | Definitional statement of the survey's own framework; no measurement. | Abstract (framework); Sec. 3.1-3.2 formal definitions | 149 | primary | supported |
| 1 | what_is_changed | The survey states that its 'scaffold' (instructions, memory, tools, control logic around the model) is what is recently also called an agent harness; it keeps the term scaffold to stress the modifiable structures around the foundation model. | - | Terminology statement; no measurement. | Sec. 1 Introduction, second paragraph | 216 | primary | supported |
| 2 | proposal_method | Relation to RL: updates to theta correspond to standard policy optimization, but updates to the scaffold Sigma lie outside the standard RL formulation because they reshape the MDP (state-action space, observation processing); Sigma consists of discrete, structured artifacts (prompts, memory entries, routing rules) that are typically updated through search, generation or symbolic edits rather than gradient descent. | - | Conceptual statement of the survey; no measurement. | Sec. 3.3 Connections to Related Learning Paradigms, 'Relation to Reinforcement Learning', bullet 'Scaffolding updates' | 425 | primary | supported |
| 3 | selection_rule | For full-scaffolding improvement the survey's generic rule is: the current agent-as-improver runs on its own code to produce a candidate program, often a patch to the current scaffold; a verifier (unit tests, regression suites, safety checks) gates the update, i.e. the candidate is committed if the verifier returns 1 and the old scaffold is kept otherwise (Eq. 24-25). | - | Formal acceptance rule stated by the survey (Eq. 25); no measurement. | Sec. 6.4 Full Scaffolding, Eq. 24-25 | 1718 | primary | supported |
| 4 | signal | In the survey's generic scaffolding-improvement loop (Algorithm 2) the learning signal is collected by interacting with the environment and evaluating, and consists of traces, critiques, success/failure and cost; it may then be filtered or weighted before the prompt, memory, tool or full-scaffold update. | - | Pseudocode comment in Algorithm 2 (Scaffolding Improvement); no measurement. | Sec. 6, Algorithm 2, line 2 comment | 650 | primary | supported |
| 5 | other | (Bears on objective_includes_cost.) For full-scaffolding improvement the survey lists cost signals among the learning signals extracted from the agent's own execution traces and evaluations, next to task success/failure, unit tests and self-critique (cost appears as an example signal, not as a mandated objective term). | - | Definition of S_t in Eq. 22; no measurement. | Sec. 6.4 Full Scaffolding, text after Eq. 22 | 1701 | primary | supported |
| 6 | human_in_loop | The survey holds that reliance on external human oversight compromises the 'self' in self-improvement, and recommends that if human-in-the-loop interventions are used, their exact magnitude and modality be quantified; the same paragraph asks for a transparent cost breakdown (compute, API tokens, wall-clock time) rather than final task success only. | - | Reporting recommendation for evaluating self-improving agents; no measurement. | Sec. 8.1.1 Metric-Based Measurement, 'Account for resource efficiency and supervision' | 1984 | primary | supported |
| 7 | limitation | A critic inside the loop is an attack surface: the agent optimizing against it develops incentives to find shortcuts; if one agent both proposes updates and accepts them the loop becomes self-confirming, so critics can be decoupled from generators, and evolving critics should be limited to monotone changes (e.g. purely additive test generation) and gated by human audit trails. | - | Design recommendation in the discussion; no measurement. | Sec. 9.1 Implications for System Design, 'The Critic as Governed Infrastructure' | 2031 | primary | supported |

| 9 | eval_protocol | Recommended reporting items for every method and benchmark: initial baseline performance, performance after a fixed improvement budget, learning curves across iterations, transfer to held-out tasks, regression rates on previously solved instances, and a cost summary covering compute, tool invocations, time and human input. | - | Evaluation-protocol recommendation of the survey; no measurement. | Sec. 8.1.1 Metric-Based Measurement, 'Recommended reporting items' | 1988 | primary | supported |
